_notes: Curation for generate_b757_map.py: what the cockpit XML cannot say, kept in one visible place.
exclude_banners: vendor banner comments whose controls are left out (circuit breakers, CDU keys, furniture, effects).
exclude_nodes: single controls left out. A name the package does not have is an error, so a stale entry cannot hide.
panels: vendor banner -> app panel name, or {name, section} when the node prefix would pick the wrong section.

node_panels: first matching {banner?, prefix?} rule wins over the banner table; {panel, section?}. A node otherwise lands in the section its prefix names (a B757_OVHD_ node in the Overhead), so a rule that moves it to another section says which.

panel_order: section -> panel names, the order the panels of that section are tabbed. The listed panels come first, in that order; the panels not listed follow alphabetically, and the run names them (a panel BlueBird adds later turns up there). A section the map does not have, a panel the section has none of, a repeat and an empty list are errors.

control_order: panel -> node names, the order the controls of that panel are tabbed. The listed controls come first, in that order; the rest follow in cockpit order. A panel no control is on, a node that is not in that panel, a repeat and an empty list are errors. Labels are made first, in cockpit order, so an order never renames or renumbers a control.
labels: node -> label, where the node name or the vendor's tooltip is wrong or unhelpful.

positions: node -> position names in value order (one per value: the names are laid onto the control's own values, so two names for a control whose values are 0 and 11 name 0 and 11), or explicit [{value, label}] when the extractor counts a value the click code never rests on (the start selectors never write 2, the chronometer ET lever skips it).

kinds: node -> toggle or button, for a control whose click code the extractor misreads. Two re-readings only: a momentary button made a toggle (its click sets its own state var by a gate, not a flip) and a select made a button (a radio-style choice that is only ever pressed). Only the kind changes (and with it the positions the generator derives: two for a toggle, none for a button, unless positions names them); the state var and the click code stay the vendor's, verbatim. The rules decide first, on the row as the extractor read it, so an entry never brings back a control they drop: it changes nothing and is only reported, like a label for a dropped node. An entry for a node the package does not have, for a control the extractor already reads that way, for any other re-reading, or for a kind the control cannot be built as (a toggle needs an L:var state), is an error.

guarded: node -> {state_var, positions, guard, guard_closed, close_sets}: a switch whose vendor click only runs while its guard is open. The extractor writes that gate as an '[if <test>] ' note in front of the click code, which is not RPN, so none of the click is kept: the control is emitted as a switch on state_var with the named positions (laid onto the control's own values, as under positions), the guard's node, the value the guard reads while closed (guard_closed) and the value closing it writes to the control (close_sets, null when closing leaves it alone), and press, release, cw and ccw are empty: the app opens the guard, writes the position and closes the guard. The guard keeps its own row. An entry takes in a control the rules leave out (the emergency lights switch) or re-reads one they keep (the stab trims), and the run names each; it never overrides exclude_nodes or an excluded banner. It is checked against the vendor's code, so that a mistyped fact or a change of BlueBird's stops the run: the click writes state_var, its gate reads the guard's var, and the guard's own click writes close_sets to the control. An entry for a node or a guard the package does not have, names that do not fit the vendor's count of positions, a positions or kinds entry for the same node, and any other control whose click code carries the gate note are errors.

direct_write: list of nodes whose vendor click code the map leaves out: the control is emitted as the rules build it (state var, kind, label, panel and positions unchanged, the positions still checked against what the vendor's code writes) and press, release, cw and ccw are empty, so the app writes the state var to the picked position, as it does for any switch with no click code. For a switch whose code cannot take a pick where it aims and writes nothing but its own L:var, and at most O:vars (the chronometer ET levers; the flight deck door switch). It is checked against the vendor's code, so that a change of BlueBird's stops the run instead of reaching the app: the click code must exist (else the entry does nothing), carry no gate note (a gated click belongs under guarded, which opens the guard first) and write nothing but the state var (another L:var, a K: or an H: event would no longer run; an O:var write is let through, because O:vars are component-local and the sim's calculator cannot set them, so the app's replay never performed it). The run names each, and what it left out. An entry for a node the package does not have or the map does not keep, a node also under guarded or kinds, a control that is not a switch or has no state var or no positions, and a click code that fails those checks are errors.

levers: node -> {state_var, positions}: a lever the rules leave out and the pilot needs (the gear lever and the flap lever: drag handles, which the extractor reads as a 'lever' with no click code a pick could replay). BlueBird publishes the state var of each with its detents ('Write a detent position'), so the entry gives the state var and the positions with their values, [{value, label}] in the order of the lever's travel (a lever's row names no values a list of names could be laid onto: the flap lever runs 0..150), and the control is emitted as a switch on state_var with press, release, cw and ccw empty: the app writes the state var to the picked position, as it does for any switch with no click code. The run names each lever it takes in. The label comes from labels, the place from the banner table or a node_panels rule, and a lever under an excluded banner (the flap lever) needs include_nodes as well, which keeps the banner's other controls out: an entry never overrides exclude_nodes or an excluded banner. It is checked against the vendor's code, so that a mistyped var or a change of BlueBird's stops the run: state_var must be an L:var the lever's whole component reads or writes (the extractor keeps that per row as _component_vars), and each position must lie in the range the lever's own code clamps to, where the extractor found one. An entry for a node the package does not have, for a node the rules keep or leave out for another reason than being a lever, for a node neither cockpit model has (keep_without_node keeps it, as for any entry), for a node also under guarded, direct_write, kinds or positions, for a state var the lever's component never touches and for a position outside the lever's range is an error.

direct_positions: node -> {state_var, positions}: a knob the rules leave out and a combo can drive (the pressurization Auto Rate knob, the three zone temperature selectors, the eight display brightness knobs). The rules drop a finite knob with more than 12 positions (Auto Rate has 131, a brightness knob 31 or 21) and every infinite knob (a zone selector wraps), and a pick by click steps would take dozens of clicks. The entry has the form of levers: state_var is the L:var the systems read and positions are [{value, label}] WITH their values, rising, and the control is emitted as a switch on state_var with press, release, cw and ccw empty: the app writes the state var to the picked position, as it does for any switch with no click code. The run names each knob it takes in. The label comes from labels, the place from the banner table or a node_panels rule; an entry never overrides exclude_nodes or an excluded banner (a knob under one needs include_nodes as well). None of the vendor's click code is kept, so the positions are not checked against the range that code clamps to: the cockpit mouse stops the brightness knobs at 30 (20 on the F/O ADI knob) while the systems take 0-40 (docs/b757/evidence/flight-12.md). It is checked against the vendor's code, so that a mistyped var or a change of BlueBird's stops the run: state_var must be an L:var the knob's whole component reads or writes (the extractor keeps that per row as _component_vars). An entry for a node the package does not have, for a node the rules keep (positions and direct_write are the keys for those) or leave out for another reason than being a knob whose positions cannot be listed (a lever has its own key), for a node curation leaves out, for a node neither cockpit model has (keep_without_node keeps it, as for any entry), for a node also under levers, guarded, direct_write, kinds or positions, for a state var the knob's component never touches, and for fewer than two positions, a repeated value or an empty label is an error.

hold_ms: node -> milliseconds: a button the cockpit shows a result for only while it is held (the fire tests, the CVR and squib tests, the other test buttons). BlueBird's template for it is the plain momentary button, which the rules keep as a button (the app presses it for 200 ms), so the entry makes it a held button (kind held) with this hold_ms: the app presses it, holds it that long and lets go (Bbs757Write.PressFor), with its press and release exactly as the rules built them. The label, panel and state var are the rules' own. A hold under 500 or over 10000 ms, or one that is not a whole number of milliseconds, is an error when the file loads. It is checked against the control the map holds, so that a change of BlueBird's stops the run: a node the package does not have or the map does not keep, a node also under kinds, a control that is not a button (a toggle, a switch, a guard, a select, or a button the extractor already reads as held, which has the hold the vendor's template gives it) and a button with no press or no release are errors. The run names each, and the hold.

keep_without_node: list of nodes kept although neither cockpit model has a node of that name. The generator reads the node names of the package's two interior models, BBS_752_PW_INTERIOR.gltf and BBS_752_RR_INTERIOR.gltf (it stops when either is missing), and leaves out every control the other rules keep whose node is in neither: a switch the cockpit does not have is noise to a pilot who cannot find it, and the run names each one. A control one model alone has says which, with (PW) or (RR) at the end of its label unless the label already does (L Fuel Control (PW)); a label that names the wrong variant stops the run. An entry here keeps a control BlueBird's published list proves real, and the run names each; it stays empty unless that list proves one. An entry for a node the package does not have, for a node a model has (it does nothing), for a node also in exclude_nodes or for one the rules leave out for another reason is an error, and so is a guarded, levers or include_nodes entry for a node no cockpit has that this list does not keep. A direct_write entry for one stops the run until it is removed, and a kinds, labels or positions entry for one changes nothing and is only reported.
spelling: vendor words repaired wherever a label is made from them (US English, vendor typos).
status: read-only L:vars the app can speak or show; positions are names for 0, 1, 2 ...

B757_OVHD_CABINALT_SWITCH is excluded (label kept for later): it is spring-loaded and gets buttons in the app (plan 12 task 3), not a row of positions. Its click code writes only 0 (anticlockwise) or 7 (clockwise), every vendor panel-state snapshot rests it at 4, the XML writes 4 back within a second of any write (XML:10128-10151), and BlueBird's WASM uses only which side of 4 the value is on: above 4 climbs, below 4 descends, 4 holds, in MAN only (Mode Select B757_OVHD_MODE_SELECT_SWITCH at 2). The vendor's OFF/AUTO/ON tips are a copy-paste. measured (docs/b757/evidence/flight-12.md): with the outflow valve L:BBS_CABIN_VALVE at 1, a 0 held for 1.2 s closed it to 0.869 and an 8 held for 1.3 s opened it to 0.963; back at 4 the valve held.

B757_OVHD_L_ENG_START_SWITCH and B757_OVHD_R_ENG_START_SWITCH: the extractor counts 6 positions, but the click code computes its values and never writes 2 (cw goes 1 to 3, ccw 3 to 1), so the list is explicit pairs without 2. All 9 vendor panel-state snapshots hold both selectors at 3, the manual's normal position is AUTO, and engine start is GND, which is ccw of AUTO. 4 OFF, 5 CONT and 6 FLT are BlueBird's names (its simvar list, cited below); unmeasured in the sim.

A banner with no entry under panels is not guessed: it is printed as a note (unmapped_banners) unless a node_panels rule names its controls. The four BBS_fuelcut_* switches (one banner is '(no banner)') are named by a node rule.

include_nodes: single controls taken in from an excluded banner BY NODE; the banner stays excluded and its other controls stay out, and the panel and section come from a node_panels rule. A name the package does not have, a node also in exclude_nodes, a node no excluded banner hides and a node the rules still drop are errors. In: BBS757_PEDESTAL_Park_Brake_Lever, BBS757_SPOILERDOWN_CLICK, BBS757_SPOILERARMED_CLICK, BBS757_SPOILERUP_CLICK (banner RIGHT WINDOW RAIN EFFECTS); ENGINE_Switch_ATDisc_1 (the left TO/GA button only; ENGINE_Switch_ATDisc_2 is not taken in) and B757_AT_DISC_1 (banner THROTTLES MAIN; B757_AT_DISC_2 is not taken in); BBS757_lever_flaps (banner RIGHT WINDOW RAIN EFFECTS: the flap lever, which the rules still drop as a lever, so it is under levers as well). All sit in Pedestal / Control stand, in the order control_order gives.

EVIDENCE for the control stand and the position names below (2026-10-25). preset = the nine vendor panel states in Data/panel_states/*.snap (cold and dark, turnaround, before start, ready for taxi, ready for takeoff, after takeoff, cruise, approach, final approach; positional arrays, but most knob states also sit in them as named L:var pairs). manual = BlueBird's v1.01 User Procedures and Complete Flight Guide. measured = read live in the sim (docs/b757/evidence/live-findings.md). unmeasured = no live read: the name rests on the sources given and goes on the in-sim plan. Names are the panel's legends as printed (capitals), as the brief spells them; a list entry 'Position N' is a position nothing names.
Position names from BlueBird's simvar list (support.bluebirdsim.com/docs/simvars, values checked against source 2026-10-21), read 2026-10-25.

PLAN 02 TASK 1 (2026-10-26): positions named from that list alone, unmeasured in the sim and with no preset or manual evidence of their own (the controls whose other notes cite the list have such evidence besides): B757_CABIN_CEILING (0 Off, 1 33%, 2 66%, 3 100%), B757_CABIN_WINDOW and B757_CABIN_ENTRY (0 Off, 1 50%, 2 100%), B757_OVHD_WARNING_IND_SWITCH (0 DIM, 11 BRT: its click code writes those two values, which the extractor takes as its positions), B757_MAIN_M_Gau_STBY_GYRO_SELECTOR (0 OFF, 1 ILS, 2 BCRS), B757_ECAM_LRAUTO_KNOB (0 L, 1 AUTO, 2 R) and B757_VC_P61_SWITCH_2, the Flight Recorder (0 ON, 1 AUTO, 2 TEST).

B757_MAIN_CHRONO_ET_SWITCH and B757_MAIN_CHRONO_ET_SWITCH_FO (L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, _FO): 0 RUN, 1 HOLD, 3 RESET, explicit pairs without 2. The list says RESET is 3 with 2 unused, and the click code agrees: the code that steps up from HOLD writes 3 straight from 1 ('1 == if{ 3 ...'), so no step from HOLD rests on 2. The cockpit's tooltip list (RUN, HOLD, RESET: three tips for four values) puts RESET at 2, which that code never writes; the generator stops on a list that names 2 instead, because 3 is then written outside the list. The code that steps down still passes through 2 on its way from 3 to 1; that stop has no name. B757_MAIN_CHRONO_SET_SWITCH and B757_MAIN_CHRONO_SET_SWITCH_FO (L:BBS_CHRONO_RIGHT_SWITCH, _FO): 0 RUN, 1 HOLD, 2 Slow slew, 3 Fast slew (the list; the vendor's tips for them repeat the ET lever's RUN, HOLD, RESET and name nothing here). Both unmeasured in the sim.

B757_VC_P61_SWITCH_3 to B757_VC_P61_SWITCH_10 are the P61 test switches: their release code writes 1, so 1 is Neutral on all of them, and the list names 0 and 2, the two tests, by the switch's label: Equip Cooling (SWITCH_3) and Yaw Damp (SWITCH_4) 'Upper test' / 'Lower test'; Wing AI Window Heat (SWITCH_6) 'Wing anti-ice test' / 'Probe heat test'; Ground Prox Hyd Gen (SWITCH_7) 'Ground proximity test' / 'Hydraulic generator test'; TO and Land Config (SWITCH_8) 'Takeoff config test' / 'Landing config test'; Air Data Stall Right (SWITCH_9) and Left (SWITCH_10) 'Air data test' / 'Stall warning test'. B757_VC_P61_SWITCH_5 (Duct Leak Fuel Qty) is the one the list gives no test names: 1 Neutral, 0 and 2 stay 'Position 0' and 'Position 2'. Unmeasured in the sim.

PLAN 02 TASK 2 (2026-10-26): labels and kinds that match the cockpit, from BBS_752_BASE_INTERIOR.xml (cited as XML:line) and BlueBird's simvar list (support.bluebirdsim.com/docs/simvars, values checked against source 2026-10-21), all unmeasured in the sim. B757_OVHD_SWITCH_GAURD is the emergency lights guard, not a passenger oxygen one: the XML says so ('OVHD SWITCH GUARD is the EMERGENCY LIGHTS GUARD', XML:11362) and passes it as the GUARD_LVAR of the emergency lights switch (BBS_B757_EMERGENCY_LIGHTS_COMPONENT, XML:8106-8110); the vendor's tip on its other row, 'RAM AIR TURBINE', and the PASS_OXY in the name of the switch it covers are copies. The list calls it 'Emergency lights guard - template and interlock', 0 = closed, 1 = open, which is what its positions say.

The hydraulic panel has two engine pumps and four electric ones. B757_OVHD_C_ENG1_HYD_PUMPS_BUTTON and B757_OVHD_C_ENG2_HYD_PUMPS_BUTTON are the center system's two electric pumps, C1 and C2 (the 757's center system has no engine pump; the XML tips read 'C ENG1 PUMP' and 'C ENG2 PUMP', XML:7085 and 7140, and the list puts them at Left / Center and Right / Center); B757_OVHD_L_ENG_ELEC_PUMPS_BUTTON and B757_OVHD_R_ENG_ELEC_PUMPS_BUTTON are the left and right electric pumps (tips 'L ENG ELEC' and 'R ENG ELEC', XML:7030 and 7250; the list: 'Hydraulic electric pump selection'). B757_OVHD_L_ENG_HYD_PUMPS_BUTTON and B757_OVHD_R_ENG_HYD_PUMPS_BUTTON stay the engine pumps, 'L ENG HYD Pumps' and 'R ENG HYD Pumps', made from their node names. The six labels differ, and the electric pumps stay in the order R, C1, C2, L (control_order, plan 12 task 4: the order they are switched on before start). B757_OVHD_XFEED_PUMPS_FWD_BUTTON and B757_OVHD_XFEED_PUMPS_AFT_BUTTON are the fuel crossfeed valve switches, not pumps: their node names and tips say pumps (XFEED PUMP FWD and AFT, XML:8585 and 8530; the list: 'Crossfeed pumps forward button'), but the circuit breakers for the same valves are named fuel_crossfeed_valve_fwd and _aft (XML:34638, 34655).

B757_GAURD_11_SWITCH and B757_GAURD_12_SWITCH are the covers of the 1 BTL and 2 BTL cargo fire buttons: the vendor's template instances of B757_PED_1BTL_CARGOFIRE_BUTTON and B757_PED_2BTL_CARGOFIRE_BUTTON name them as their GUARD_NODE_ID (XML:15975 and 16013), so they read '1 BTL Cargo Fire Guard' and '2 BTL Cargo Fire Guard' after the buttons' own labels. The list has no row for either guard; the vendor's disabled earlier components tip them 'FWD CARGO' and 'AFT CARGO'.

B757_MCP_btn_autopilot_disengage: 0 Up, 1 Down. Its click flips its own var and passes it on to K:AUTOPILOT_DISENGAGE_SET ('if{ 1 (>K:AUTOPILOT_DISENGAGE_SET) } els{ 0 (>K:AUTOPILOT_DISENGAGE_SET) }'), so 1 is the bar down, which disengages the autopilot, and 0 the bar up; its animation names no positions and the list has no row for it. BBS757_THRREF_CLICK (L:BBS757_THRREF_PULL): 0 In, 1 Pulled; the list: 'Manual EPR-reference mode', 1 = pulled/manual, 0 = pushed/manual off. B757_MCP_AP_SPD_HOLD_SW writes L:B757_MCP_IAS_MACH_KNOB_BUTTON, which the list calls the 'Speed intervention command' (write 1 to request it, 0 = idle): the push of the IAS/MACH knob, so it reads 'Speed Intervene', not 'AP SPD Hold'.

BBS757_FIREHANDLE1_CLICK3, the APU fire handle, is a toggle (kinds) on L:B757_APUFIRE_SWITCH, its pulled state, as the engine handles are on L:B757_ENGFIRE_1_SWITCH and _2_ (the list: 'Apufire switch', 0 = normal, 1 = fire handle pulled): 0 In, 1 Pulled. Its click writes 1 when the handle is unlocked (L:BBS757_FIREUNLOCK3) or the APU fire is active and 0 otherwise, a gate and not a flip, so the extractor read a momentary button with no state to show; the app now reads the handle before it presses. The press also has a slip of the vendor's own, which the replay test of plan 02 task 6 found: right after the rotation test it runs 'and' with nothing to combine it with (XML:15767-15768; the engine handles run their 'and' after the 'or' that follows the unlock and fire tests, XML:15572-15578). What the sim does with it is unmeasured: if an 'and' that lacks an operand reads it as 0, which is what the replay test assumes, the rotation plays no part and the handle pulls on the unlock or the fire alone; if the sim stops at the 'and', the press does nothing. The slip is recorded here and not under _suspected_slips, which lists what the generator's own check finds (a set with no variable type, a closing brace nothing opened). The 14 microphone selects, B757_PED_AUDIO_1_MIC_L_LIGHT to _INT_LIGHT and the seven of B757_PED_AUDIO_2_MIC_*_LIGHT, are buttons (kinds): a click sets that microphone to 1 and the panel's other six to 0, so a combo of Off and On could never reach Off. The list calls each a 'microphone selector' (0 = deselected, 1 = selected; 'a 0-to-1 transition selects the transmitter').

PLAN 02 TASK 3 (2026-10-26): the emergency lights switch and the two stab trim cutouts are guarded, from BBS_752_BASE_INTERIOR.xml (cited as XML:line) and BlueBird's simvar list (support.bluebirdsim.com/docs/simvars, values checked against source 2026-10-21). B757_OVHD_PASS_OXY_Toggle_Switch_CLICK is the emergency lights switch (label Emergency Lights; BBS_B757_EMERGENCY_LIGHTS_COMPONENT, XML:8106-8120; the PASS_OXY in its node name is a copy, as for its guard): its state is L:B757_OVHD_PASS_OXY_Toggle_Switch_CLICK, 0 OFF, 1 ARMED, 2 ON (the list; its click steps '1 + 2 min' and '1 - 0 max', XML:1504 and 1507, which is why the extractor read a switch with three positions, and its animation reads an O: var, which is why the rules left it out). Its guard is B757_OVHD_SWITCH_GAURD, its own L:var (XML:1361): the click runs only while that reads 1 (XML:1502), so 1 is open and 0 is closed (guard_closed 0; the list: 0 = closed, 1 = open). Closing the guard writes 1, ARMED, to the switch: the guard's click writes its RESET_VALUE 1 (XML:1375-1378 and 8118) and the switch's own update code forces 1 while the guard reads 0 (XML:1532), so close_sets is 1. B757_Stab_trim_C_toggle_switch_CLICK and B757_Stab_trim_R_toggle_switch_CLICK are the stab trim cutouts (labels Stab Trim C Cutout and Stab Trim R Cutout; BBS757_STAB_TRIM_CUTOUTS, XML:15380-15408): their states are L:B757_Stab_trim_C_toggle_switch_CLICK and L:B757_Stab_trim_R_toggle_switch_CLICK, 0 NORMAL, 1 CUTOUT (the list; the click toggles 0 and 1, XML:1426), behind B757_AISLE_STAND_STAB_1_GAURD_SWITCH and B757_AISLE_STAND_STAB_2_GAURD_SWITCH, each its own L:var (XML:1361); the click runs only while its guard reads 1 (XML:1424), and closing a guard writes its RESET_VALUE 0, NORMAL, to the switch (XML:15385 and 15393), so close_sets is 0. The extractor had read the stab trims as toggles whose press began with the gate note (not valid RPN, and its 'On' was CUTOUT). measured (docs/b757/evidence/live-findings.md, docs/b757/spec-gaps.md 3.3): the emergency lights switch reads 1 with its guard 0, the stab trims 0 with their guards 0, none changed. The sim's own gate is in the click, which the app no longer replays. Plan 03's guarded writer (Bbs757Guarded, on B757) opens the guard before it writes any position but the one closing the guard sets (ARMED, NORMAL), and reaches that one by closing the guard. Plan 03 measured it on the ground (docs/b757/evidence/flight-03.md, 2026-10-26): a write to the emergency lights switch (2) and to stab trim C (1) holds with the guard open, and the guard's own press then writes ARMED and NORMAL back, as close_sets says; stab trim R is the same template and was not tried. Behind a closed guard the two kinds differ, unmeasured in the sim: the emergency lights switch's update code forces its var to 1 while the guard reads 0 (XML:1532), but the stab trims' template gates in the click only (XML:1424) and its update (XML:1447-1455) just sets the var to 0 once at load, so nothing reverts a stab trim write made behind a closed guard.

PLAN 02 TASK 4 (2026-10-26, ruling R10): B757_MAIN_CHRONO_ET_SWITCH and B757_MAIN_CHRONO_ET_SWITCH_FO are direct_write: the map holds none of their click code and the app writes L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH (_FO) to the picked value. Read from the vendor's code (BBS_752_BASE_INTERIOR.xml:26725-26735 and 28542-28552), unmeasured in the sim: the clockwise code lowers the value one step, '(L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, enum) -- d 0 < if{ 0 } (>L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, enum)', so 3 goes to 2 to 1 to 0, and the anticlockwise code raises it but jumps HOLD straight to RESET, '(L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, enum) 1 == if{ 3 (>L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, enum) } els{ (L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, enum) ++ d 3 > if{ 3 } (>L:BBS_CHRONO_LEFT_SWITCH, enum) }', so 0 goes to 1 to 3. The positions are 0 RUN, 1 HOLD and 3 RESET, with 2 unused (BlueBird's list; task 1 left it out). The map's cw was that clockwise code, so the app's step up lowered the value; swapping cw and ccw would fix the direction and not the steps: a step down from RESET still lands on 2, which is no position, and the app then refuses every later pick. The vendor code writes nothing but that one L:var (the generator checks that on every run), so writing the picked value directly loses nothing, and it also takes a pick from a lever a cockpit click has left on 2. The positions stay checked against that code: a list that names RESET at 2 still stops the run.

PLAN 02 TASK 5 (2026-10-26, ruling R65): the map holds only controls the cockpit has. Read from the package's two interior models, BBS_752_PW_INTERIOR.gltf (3104 nodes) and BBS_752_RR_INTERIOR.gltf (3116 nodes, 3094 of them in both), by node name, whole and as written (no node of either has one of the names below in another case). The package ships six interior models, the standard, AWE and no-cab one of each engine (BBS_752_PW_INTERIOR_AWE.gltf, BBS_752_PW_INTERIOR_NC.gltf, BBS_752_RR_INTERIOR_AWE.gltf and BBS_752_RR_INTERIOR_NC.gltf besides the two above); the generator reads the two standard ones. They agree on every control node: checked on 2026-10-26, each of the 405 controls of the map (the two levers of task 7 among them) and each of the 22 named below has a node in the AWE and the no-cab model exactly where it has one in the standard model of the same engine. (The two low-detail LOD01 interiors lack most control nodes and are not read.) Of the 425 controls the other rules kept, 395 have a node in both models, 2 in the PW model only, 6 in the RR model only and 22 in neither. In the PW model only: BBS_fuelcut_PW1 and BBS_fuelcut_PW2, whose labels already end (PW). In the RR model only: BBS_fuelcut_RR1 and BBS_fuelcut_RR2, whose labels already end (RR); B757_OVHD_L_ELEC-ENG-CONT_BUTTON and B757_OVHD_R_ELEC-ENG-CONT_BUTTON, which now read L ELEC ENG Cont (RR) and R ELEC ENG Cont (RR); and their guards B757_GAURD_1_SWITCH and B757_GAURD_2_SWITCH, Elec Eng Cont 1 Guard (RR) and Elec Eng Cont 2 Guard (RR).
